title: MULE - A Match 3 love letter to Resident Evil
author: poundofcake
selftext:
It's 2:40AM and the Parasol Ashgrove Research Campus has gone dark. Early reports say Dr. Voss went rogue and released a virus. The last operative sent hasn't checked in either.

Infiltrate, find Dr. Voss, secure whatever he was working on, and escape through the access tunnel to meet your contact.

\---------------------------------------------------

I created a match 3 survival-horror game for a game jam with a mobile crafting theme. It started out as a short RE4 style case crafting game, that quickly blew out in scope to MULE.

This is the most ambitious game I've made thus far and it's crazy how I could orchestrate agents to fill out roles I needed to finish before the deadline. Happy to share the process if anyone is interested and would love any feedback.

It's free to play on itch: [https://sykoramade.itch.io/mule](https://sykoramade.itch.io/mule)

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Conceptually, I really like this.

Experientially, I have two major gripes, one of them just a matter of personal taste:

1. (Not a matter of taste) - because of the vertical arrangement of the puzzle pieces well below the display of what is happening, I spend most of the experience focused on the pieces and cannot even keep what is happening in my peripheral vision. I'm playing this on PC; I suspect a screen designed for the vertical experience would give a much better experience, but that's not a great excuse for a multi-platform game. Either the layout should be able to work with my platform, or the game shouldn't be available on my platform.
2. (Personal thing) I dislike the meta-puzzles. The actual puzzles that drive the primary experience are great, but the meta-puzzles feel like the only reason they are here is that RE had them; ergo, your game should have them. For me, they don't fit the mood of the game as a much lighter experience that already has a very engaging core loop without also requiring the player to do a 'figure out how to unlock this door' game. The old RE games only had that shit in them to pad out the playtime, and it's not needed here

2.5) Where is my intellectually distinct Not Jill Valentine waifu? ;.; EDIT: NVM! I FOUND HER!
